items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...he says that the flavor of the great Thelonious Monk permeates the proceedings of Riff Raff... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, maybe he's talking in terms of the same kind of feel, you might say.

ctx.x: Riff Raff? I can't see that. I don't believe that ... I don't know what he means by that. Riff Raff was just one of my ideas, and we run it over. And that was it. I had something to do with somebody else, I believe, in later years. After I played with him. But Leon Blevins had a part in that.

Well it could be then, I don't know how he means that, either, because he says that the flavor of the great Thelonious Monk permeates the proceedings of Riff Raff, and was most reminiscent of (inaudible) Well, You Needn't;"
Well, maybe he's talking in terms of the same kind of feel, you might say.
